result.title: Any3R: Feedforward 3D Reconstruction from Any Camera Type
result.summary: Geometry foundation models recover camera poses and dense geometry from a set of images with a feed-forward network, but they expect pinhole images. That assumption is inside the backbone too: the positional encoding and the training loss both bind an image position to a direction in space, and both depend on the lens. We condition both on the dense ray field, the unit direction through every pixel, which describes any central camera without a lens type, distortion coefficients or a bound on field of view. Angular coordinates give the rotary encoding the measured ray angle of each patch, evaluated per view, and solid-angle weighting scales the point loss by the area each pixel covers on the sphere, so neither the encoding nor the supervision depends on the lens. Any3R is therefore a feed-forward model that takes any central camera, and is robust to mixing many camera types per scene, with no retraining per lens. On a benchmark of thirteen central cameras across three datasets, where every method reconstructs with its own predicted camera poses, it is the most consistently accurate method. Any3R enables scalable 3D reconstruction from heterogeneous crowdsourced and archival imagery collections sourced across diverse camera types. Project page: https://jingong-chen.github.io/Any3R/

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Any3R：把位置编码与训练损失都条件化在稠密光线场（每像素的单位方向）上，用角度坐标驱动 rotary encoding、以立体角加权点损失，使前馈几何基础模型无需镜头类型或畸变参数即可处理任意中心相机，并稳健应对同场景混合相机类型。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文用光线方向而非镜头参数定义像素与空间方向的对应，并据此改造编码与监督，可能为视觉 token 如何在内部状态中保留几何与细粒度空间信息提供可核查线索；但它本身不做多模态推理，与 LVR 的状态生成和停止决策联系较远。
